turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm here because my family thinks I'm doing too much. They made me come in. But honestly, I just feel like I'm the only one with enough drive to actually get things done. We're moving, and I'm handling all of that, plus I'm rebuilding the new garage so it's done right. I've also been organizing a lot of things over at the church. And on top of it all, I'm still working—showing the younger guys at the plant how the mixing and blending ought to be handled. I just have a lot going on, and I'm getting it all done, but everyone else seems to think it's a problem.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient demonstrates inflated self-confidence by stating they are the only one with enough drive to get things done and that they need to show others how to do their jobs.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a significant increase in goal-directed activities across multiple areas of life, including handling a move, rebuilding a garage, organizing at church, and taking on extra roles at work.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you been needing much less sleep than usual lately?
turns.patient_response: Well, I wouldn't say I need less sleep, exactly. I just haven't had time for it, what with the move and the garage and everything else. I'll sleep when the work is done.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep, attributing their lack of sleep to being busy with tasks rather than a decreased need.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe you have any special powers or abilities that other people don't have?
turns.patient_response:
Special powers? No, I don't... I don't have magic or anything like that. I'm just a hard worker. 

I've been around a long time, so I know how things ought to be done. Like I said, with the mixing and blending at the plant, I just have the experience the younger guys don't. It's not a superpower to just have some common sense and the drive to actually put your head down and do the work. I'm just capable, that's all.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having special powers or magic, indicating an absence of grandiose delusions.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient denies having superpowers or special abilities, attributing his competence to experience and hard work rather than grandiosity.

turns.doctor_question: Lately, have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or especially irritable?
turns.patient_response:
I guess you could say a bit of both. I mean, I feel great—like I'm ten feet tall and can take on anything right now. But... yeah, I have been irritable, too. 

It just feels like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or get out of my way. I’ll go right from joking around and feeling on top of the world to snapping at my wife or my boy just because they asked some little question. It just gets under my skin when people slow me down.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly confirms feeling both unusually high ('feeling on top of the world') and irritable.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient describes feeling 'ten feet tall and can take on anything right now,' indicating inflated self-esteem and grandiosity.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient reports low frustration tolerance and snappiness, stating they snap at their family over 'some little question' and get irritated when slowed down.

turns.doctor_question: Has this caused serious problems in your life lately, like trouble at work or major conflict at home?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, it has caused some problems. I ended up getting pulled from work recently. There was a safety incident at the plant, and they told me I had to step away for a bit. 

And at home... things have been rough. My wife and the rest of the family, they've basically stopped trusting me with things. They don't want me making decisions about our money, they don't want me driving, and they've kind of taken over the whole moving process. They say things just got too out of hand with me running it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: No, I can't say I have. I mean, I've had days where I felt a bit down or tired, sure, just like anybody else. But nothing like that. Not two straight weeks of feeling depressed all day. I've always been more of a doer, you know? Keeping busy. So, no, I haven't really dealt with that kind of deep depression you're talking about.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies ever having a two-week period of feeling depressed most of the day.

turns.doctor_question: Before this current stretch, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt unusually energized or high like this?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good, you know, got a lot done at the plant or around the house, but... nothing quite like this. This is the first time I've felt this revved up, where it's actually causing all these problems with my family and my job. So, no, never anything like this before.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?
turns.patient_response: No, no, I haven't had anything like that. I'm not seeing things or hearing voices or anything. My mind is just... going fast, you know? But my eyes and ears are working fine. Just the regular stuff that's actually there.

symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient describes their mind as 'going fast', which indicates racing thoughts.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies seeing things or hearing voices that others do not.
